Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the run-chase! The Irish players are out there in the middle. Tadiwanashe Marumani and Innocent Kaia are the openers for Zimbabwe. Harry Tector will start with the ball. Here we go...
… THE RUN CHASE …

Now the total is not a big one but the wicket is quite slow, if Ireland manage to take early wickets, it won't be easy for the home side to chase this down. Zimbabwe on the other hand, will want to make full use of the Powerplay. Stay tuned for the chase in a bit.

Zimbabwe started off really well with the ball but leaked a little too many runs in the middle overs. They did well to drag things back in the end but they will probably a little disappointed as they would have loved to keep Zimbabwe under the 130-run mark after the start they had got with the ball. It was yet again the spinners who were brilliant, the likes of Wellington Masakadza and Burl were really good and they were well supported by Wesley Madhevere who got two important wickets.

Zimbabwe will be pretty happy with how they have bowled but Ireland will fell they have recovered well and got themselves to a competitive total. Let me remind you, they were three down for not a lot but but then, Tector and Campher played really well to steady the ship. Both though fell in quick succession. However, Dockrell and Adair managed to take their side to over the 140-run mark.

A bye to end the innings! A slower shortish delivery, around off. Hand tries to heave it towards the leg side but misses. The ball goes off the bounce to the keeper and a bye is taken. Ireland finish with 141/9 at the end of their 20 overs!

Back of a length, on middle and leg. Hand tries to clip it but misses. The ball goes off his pads towards short fine leg. The fielder there has a shy at the batter's end as the batters try to steal a leg bye but misses and an overthrow is taken.
A fuller delivery on middle. White works it to square leg for a single.

OUT! CAUGHT! He holes out in the deep this time! It is not easy to hit boundaries here but Barry McCarthy has no choice and he tries tonk this slower length delivery down the ground. He, however, hits it flat and straight to long on where Wellington Masakadza takes a fine catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Wellington Masakadza b Luke Jongwe

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This is full and outside off. Barry McCarthy clears his front leg and slams it over the cover fence for a maximum.

OUT! CAUGHT! George Dockrell departs now! A low full toss on off. It was there for Dockrell to hit. However, he fails to get the timing right again and hits it aerially and straight to long off. Wesley Madhevere takes an easy catch and the home crowd rejoices. Barry McCarthy is the next man in.
Commentary.Howout: c Wesley Madhevere b Luke Jongwe

Commentary.Commentary: OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Chatara with a superb yorker and Ireland lose their seventh! Nails a yorker on off. Adair who was struggling to get his timing right in this innings fails to get his bat down in time as the ball knocks over the off pole. Brilliant bowling and this has been a very good bowling performance by the home team. Fionn Hand is the next man in.
Serves it fuller and on leg. Dockrell flicks it to deep square leg for just a single.
Shortish and on off. Dockrell pulls it towards cow corner and comes back for the second run.
On a length and outside off. Dockrell shimmies down the track and slaps it to deep cover-point for a couple.
A fullish delivery on off. Adair makes room and slices it to sweeper cover for a single.
Back of a length and around off. Adair goes for a wild swing across the line but misses.
Couple of runs to end the over! Bowls it fuller and on leg. Dockrell makes room and forces it left of long off for a couple.
On a length, on off. Adair heaves it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Again no timing here! A fullish delivery on off. Dockrell tries to tonk it down the ground but gets the bottom of his blade. The ball goes aerially and falls well short of long on. Just a single.
Serves a fuller delivery on off. Adair hits it hard to long on for a single.
Bowls it fuller and around off. Adair drives it wide of long off for a couple.
A slower short delivery on off. Dockrell pulls it to long on for a single.
Bowls it fuller and on middle. Adair heaves it wide of long on for a couple.
A flatter delivery on middle. Dockrell fends it towards the off side for a single.
Adair shimmies down the track and the length is pulled back a bit, on off. Adair pushes it towards the off side and takes a single.
Bowls it fuller and on middle. Dockrell drills it to long off for a single.
FOUR! This man is key now for Ireland! A fuller delivery, around off. Dockrell makes room and plays an inside out drive over extra cover for a boundary.
Shorter and on off. Dockrell makes room and slaps it down the ground for a couple.
FOUR! Cut away! Shorter and outside off, this is cut through point for a boundary.
Shorter and outside off, Mark Adair plays it thorugh point for two.

OUT! LEADING EDGE AND TAKEN AGAIN! Tossed up leg stump, Neil Rock looks to work it on the leg side, this turns away, goes off the leading edge and it is an easy catch for Craig Ervine at covers. Ireland are losing their way now!
Commentary.Howout: c Craig Ervine b Ryan Burl

Commentary.Commentary: On off, this is played through covers for one more.
Lands safe! Outside off, tossed up, this is hit through covers for one.
On off, this is pushed through covers for one.
Bowls it fuller and outside off. Quicker again and Rock who tries to drive it, gets beaten.
Bowls it fuller and on off. George Dockrell drives it to long off for a single.
On middle and fuller. Rock works it to mid-wicket for a single.

OUT! BOWLED! Wesley Madhevere strikes and gets a big wicket of Tector! Tector shimmies down the track as Wesley Madhevere fires a full delivery on middle. It yorks Tector and he fails to get his bat down in time as the ball knocks over the stumps. The 'round the wicket angle also seems to have done the trick here. Neil Rock is the next man in.
A fuller delivery on off. George Dockrell drives it to long off for a single.
A full toss on leg. Tector forces it to long on for a single.
Flatter and quicker outside off. Tector square drives it to sweeper cover for a single.
On off, this is played through covers for one.
Another single as this is hit through covers.
On off, this is pushed through covers for one.

OUT! LEADING EDGE AND TAKEN! The stand that was going along so nicely has been broken! The googly, on the pads, Curtis Campher looks to work it on the leg side but this goes off the leading edge on the off side. The keeper takes it nicely. Can Zimbabwe build on this now?
Commentary.Howout: c Clive Madande b Ryan Burl

Commentary.Commentary: On off, tossed up, this is hit towards cover for one.
Around off, Harry Tector plays it through point and takes one.
A single as this is worked towards mid-wicket.
Steps out and then hits it down to long off for one.
Shortish and into the body, Curtis Campher looks to pull, this goes off the inside edge towards fine leg for one.
Slightly shorter and on middle, this is pushed through covers for one.
FOUR! Up and over! That is a top shot! Fuller and on off, Harry Tector makes room and lifts it over mid off for a boundary.
This is fuller and outside off. Tector tries to sweep it again but misses again. The ball goes off his pads towards the off side and a leg bye is taken.
Shortish length again on middle. Campher knocks it down the ground for a single.
Touch shorter and on middle. Tector punches it to long on for a single.
Tossed up and outside off. Tector plays a lofted  drive over extra cover and comes back for the second run.
Bowls it fuller and around off. Tector tries to sweep it but misses. The ball hits his pads and there is an appeal but the impact is outside off.
Bowls it fuller and on off. Campher drives it to long off for a single.
WIDE! Full and drifting down the leg side. Campher tries to sweep it but misses.
Tossed up delivery on off. Campher drives it to mid off for a single.
Two! Around off, this is played through point for two.
A single as this is played through covers.
On off, this is pushed towards cover for one.
Around off, this is guided to point.
Another dot! On off, this is pushed to cover.
DROPPED! That should have been taken! On middle, this is hammered back to the bowler. He gets two hands to it but spills it.
Two! On off, this is guided through point for two.
A single as this is pushed through cover.
Another dot as this is played out back to the bowler.
On off, this is pushed to cover.
On middle, this is flicked through mid-wicket for one.
On middle, defended.
Shorter and around off, this is played through point for one.
On middle, this is flicked on the leg side and a run is taken.
Another single as this is worked through mid-wicket.
On middle, this is worked through square leg for one.
WIDE! Down the leg side, wided.
FOUR! Deft! The paddle scoop comes out and it is played very fine, it races away to the fine leg fence. Really good shot.
Shorter and on the body, this is pulled down to fine leg for one.
Curtis Campher steps out, the length is shortened a touch, he looks to pull but misses and gets hit on the body.
Shorter and angled into the body, this is worked through square leg for one.
Angled into the pads, Curtis works it through square leg and gets to the other end.
On middle, this is worked through square leg for one.
FOUR! Tucked away nicely and the 50 is up! On the pads, this is worked fine on the leg side for a boundary. A welcome one.
Shortish and on middle. Tector works it to long on for a single.
Another run as this is played through point.
Another single as this is worked through square leg.
On off, this is pushed down to long off for one.
On off, this is played through covers for one.
Two more! On middle, this is pushed down to long on for two.
Confusion but no harm done! On middle, this is worked to square leg. Harry Tector wants a run but is sent back.
NOT OUT! Curtis Campher is in! On off, this is guided to short third man. They take off. The fielder hits the stumps at the keeper's end. It is taken upstairs but replays show that Curtis is in.
WIDE! Down the leg side and Tector who tries to flick it, misses.
A fullish delivery on off. Tector drives it to the cover fielder.
FOUR! Pulled away! Good effort in the deep but in vain! Shorter and on middle, this is pulled through mid-wicket and this one races away to the fence.
On off, this is guided to point.
A single as this is pushed through covers.
Two! On middle, this is pulled through mid-wicket for a couple.
On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for one.
On off, this is pushed to cover.
Outside off, this is carved over point for a couple.
WIDE! Curtis Campher looks to be innovative, he tries to play the paddle scoop but this is bowled down the leg side. He misses.
Length and on off, Harry Tector plays it towards point and gets to the other end.
Two more! On off, this is pushed through covers for two.
EDGY FOUR! Ireland won't mind how they come as long as they do! Flatter and on off, Curtis Campher looks to cut but it goes off the outside edge down tot he third man fence.

OUT! TIMBER! Wellington Masakadza also strikes in the first over itself! That is a brilliant delivery! A yorker on middle, Andy Balbirnie is late in getting his bat down and the leg stump is uprooted. Zimbabwe all over their opposition. The crowd here is enjoying it.
Three more! On middle, Harry Tector pulls it through mid-wicket for three.
On middle, this is pushed down to long off for one.

A better throw and Andy Balbirnie was a goner! This is shorter and outside off, it is cut to point. They take off. This is hit straight at the fielder but his throw is a wayward one and hence, it is an easy single in the end.
This is fired on middle, Harry Tector walks across and sweeps but to square leg.
A dot to end a successful over from Tendai Chatara! On off, this is defended.
Another single as this is nudged around the corner.
Angled into the pads, Andy Balbirnie looks to flick but misses, it hits the pad and rolls on the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Tector is off the mark! Length and on off, this is guided down to third man for one.

OUT! TAKEN! Straight to the fielder! Stephen Doheny departs for another low score! This is full and on middle, way too full to get under. Stephen Doheny looks to go over mid off but fails to get the elevation he wanted. It is an easy catch for Wellington Masakadza there. Two wickets in the first three overs and Zimbabwe right on top. Harry Tector walks out to the middle now.
Commentary.Howout: c Wellington Masakadza b Tendai Chatara

Commentary.Commentary: On off, Stephen Doheny pushes it to covers.
A dot to end! On off, this is guided to point.
That is wonderfully timed again! Length and on off, this is pushed down the ground through mid off for two.
FOUR! That is very nicely played! Plays it with the angle, makes room, stays leg side and with the angle, lofts this over cover for a boundary.
Almost plays it on! Shorter and outside off, Andy Balbirnie looks to push at it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Back of a length and on off, this is pushed to cover.
Shorter and on middle, Stephen Doheny nudges it to mid-wicket for one.
Richard Ngarava to start from the other end.
On middle, Stephen Doheny is off the mark as he works this through square leg.

OUT! TAKEN! The ploy to begin with a spinner has worked wonders! The star of the last game walks back in the first over! This is tossed up outside off, Ross Adair looks to go big but this goes more off the outer half over cover. It is taken by Ervine who runs back. A good catch from him and that is the perfect start for Zimbabwe. Stephen Doheny walks in next.
Commentary.Howout: c Craig Ervine b Wesley Madhevere

Commentary.Commentary: On middle, this is nudged towards mid-wicket for one.
Shorter and on middle, this is pushed down to long on for one. Ross Adair is off the mark!
Flatter and on off, Ross pushes it to covers.
Ireland are underway! On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
We are all set to begin! The Zimbabwean players are out there in the middle. Andy Balbirnie and Ross Adair are the openers for Ireland. Wesley Madhevere to start with the ball. Here we go...

Andy Balbirnie says the trend has been to bowl first but he hopes they can do well with the bat. States they play a lot of cricket in the world and it is about adapting. Adds the last game was a memorable one. Informs they have three changes.

Craig Ervine says bowling first seems to be the trend and he prefers chasing. States they were on track to get to 160 in the last game and he feels that is a good score. Informs Sean Williams is out and Tony Munyonga comes in and Brad Evans sits out for Luke Jongwe!
PITCH REPORT - The wicket should be the best one to bat on so far, there could be a little bit of spin and bat first is the way to go.

Ireland (PLAYING XI) - Andrew Balbirnie (C), Ross Adair, Stephen Doheny (WK), Harry Tector, George Dockrell, Curtis Campher, Neil Rock (In place of Tyrone Kane), Mark Adair, Fionn Hand, Benjamin White (In place of Gareth Delany) , Barry McCarthy (In place of Graham Hume).

Zimbabwe (PLAYING XI) - Tadiwanashe Marumani, Innocent Kaia (WK), Craig Ervine (C), Wesley Madhevere, Tony Munyonga (In place of Sean Williams), Ryan Burl, Clive Madande, Luke Jongwe (In place of Brad Evans), Wellington Masakadza, Richard Ngarava, Tendai Chatara.
TOSS - Zimbabwe HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO FIELD!

Zimbabwe had very little chance of winning the match since the Irish bowlers were efficient and the batsmen too performed well. However, this is where things start to get interesting. The final game will now determine which team is the true king after a one-all series. Can Ireland win it? Or will Zimbabwe recover to beat the Irish team? We shall find out together. Toss and team news in a bit.

Hello and a warm welcome to the Harare Sports Club as Zimbabwe takes on Ireland in the series decider. So, the series is all squared up for now as it was the Zimbabwe side that took the honors in the opening contest, and Ireland roared back strongly to clinch the second game. In a do-or-die match, a spirited Ireland side showed grit and determination and thrashed Zimbabwe by 6 wickets. It was a game where the visitors hardly put a foot wrong and showed the home side why they are a tough side to crack. The home side will now look to win this one in front of their passionate crowd.
... MATCH DAY ...

The cricketing action in Zimbabwe continues, and it is time for the T20I series decider between Zimbabwe and Ireland at the Harare Sports Club. This has been an entertaining series so far, and it hangs in the balance with both teams having the opportunity to seal it in the third and final T20I. The hosts put on a dominant performance in the first game, where their bowlers set up the game for them, and in the end they got over the line in a comfortable manner. However, in the previous game, they couldn't replicate that and let the Irish level the series. Their batting has been a little bit inconsistent, and they will need to convert their starts into big scores. Their skipper, Craig Ervine, Innocent Kaia, and Sean Williams, will need to take on more responsibility. Ryan Burl has shown his all-around abilities in the absence of their star performer, Sikandar Raza. They have two quality pacers in Tendai Chatara and Richard Ngarava, and if everything goes according to plan, they should get over the line and win the series. Ireland, on the other hand, showed their grit and determination as they came back hard in the second game after a loss to level the series. They looked like a complete unit and were better in every department. Ross Adair was their match-winner with a brilliant half-century, but the credit also goes to their bowlers. Ireland had a lot of options in their bowling department, and they used that to perfection. They have shown us in the 2022 T20 World Cup that on their day they can beat any team, and the key players for them will be Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, and George Dockrell. They will be high on confidence from their victory in the previous match and will hope to do something similar to win this series. Whatever the result might be, we can expect a thrilling contest. Let's see who comes out on top.
